tier1.text: Each lunate helps form the wrist joint with the radius, the forearm bone on the thumb side. At this joint, the rounded lunate meets a shallow hollow at the end of the radius. The lunate is one of eight carpal bones, the small bones of the wrist. The name lunate means “moon-shaped,” and this bone sits between the scaphoid and triquetrum bones.

sentences.text: Each lunate helps form the wrist joint with the radius, the forearm bone on the thumb side.

quotes.quote: wrist joint, located between the forearm and hand regions of the upper limb; articulation formed proximally by the distal end of the radius and the fibrocartilaginous pad that unites the distal radius and ulna bone, and distally by the scaphoid, lunate, and triquetrum carpal bones
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: radius: bone located along the lateral (thumb) side of the forearm

sentences.text: At this joint, the rounded lunate meets a shallow hollow at the end of the radius.

quotes.quote: Another example is the radiocarpal joint of the wrist, between the shallow depression at the distal end of the radius bone and the rounded scaphoid, lunate, and triquetrum carpal bones.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The lunate is one of eight carpal bones, the small bones of the wrist.

quotes.quote: carpal bone: one of the eight small bones that form the wrist and base of the hand; these are grouped as a proximal row consisting of (from lateral to medial) the scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, and pisiform bones
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The name lunate means “moon-shaped,” and this bone sits between the scaphoid and triquetrum bones.

quotes.quote: The bones in the proximal row, running from the lateral (thumb) side to the medial side, are the scaphoid (“boat-shaped”), lunate (“moon-shaped”), triquetrum (“three-cornered”), and pisiform (“pea-shaped”) bones.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.
